transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher first. Lay down towels and have a shallow tray ready, as several litres of water may escape. Wear gloves to protect against broken glass in the sump. Take out the lower rack, then twist and lift out the filter from the bottom of the tub. Rinse it under the tap and clear any food, grease or debris from the sump underneath. You can see a helpful picture in the app. Was the filter or sump blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

Thanks, I've had a look. The filter was already clean, and so was the area underneath. There's just a small amount of clean water sitting in the sump under the filter, roughly a cupful. Is that normal?

Thanks for checking the filter. Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher before starting. With the filter still out and the machine unplugged, wear gloves to protect against broken glass in the sump. Bail out any standing water using a cup and sponge. Locate the small pump cover on the sump, lift its clip, and look underneath with a torch for debris like glass or stones. Gently turn the impeller with your finger only; do not use tools inside the housing. Did you find something caught (and remove it), is the impeller broken, or does it turn freely with nothing there?

I haven't opened the pump cover yet, as the machine is only two weeks old and I'd rather not take it apart. The water is clean, there are no error codes, and it cleans and dries fine. Is a cupful in the sump after every cycle actually a problem?

Thanks for letting me know you’d rather not check the impeller yourself. Before we look at the drain hose, please switch the machine off and unplug it first. Turn the water off at the tap the appliance is connected to as well. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Next, check the grey drain hose from the back of the dishwasher to the sink waste isn’t kinked or squashed — especially where it runs behind the plinth or under the sink. Was the hose kinked or blocked (and is it clear now), or is it running freely?
I had a look at the hose without pulling it out: it loops up under the sink and I can't see any kinks. The water in the sump is the same the next day, not rising. Is that enough to say it's fine?

Thanks for checking that. Before you start, please switch the machine off and unplug it first. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Under the sink, look where the drain hose joins the waste. On a newly fitted sink waste the little blanking plug inside the spigot has to be cut out, and the sink trap mustn't be blocked — run the sink tap and check it drains freely. Was the blanking plug still in or the trap blocked (and is it cleared now), or is the connection fine?

I'm not sure how to check the blanking plug without pulling the hose off the spigot, and I'd rather not disconnect a new install. The hose loops up under the sink with no kinks, and the machine seems to empty the main tub fine. Is a cupful in the sump after every cycle normal for these?

Thanks for confirming the drain hose is clear. Please put the filter back in place and close the door. Select cancel or a drain/rinse programme and let it run for a couple of minutes, listening near the bottom of the machine. If any water has reached the plug or socket, don't touch it — tell me straight away instead. Did the water pump away this time?
I haven't run a drain cycle yet. The main tub is empty after each cycle, it's only the cupful under the filter that stays. Should I expect that water to pump away on a drain programme?

Thanks for letting me know. No problem if you haven’t had a chance yet. With the filter back in, close the door, choose cancel or a drain/rinse programme and let it run for a couple of minutes, listening near the bottom of the machine. If any water has reached the plug or socket, don't touch it — tell me straight away instead. Did the water pump away this time?
